Mid-air, the women cried out the name of Jesus. The car seemed to halt, then dropped straight down and landed softly. The next week he was back in church, and he has kept coming.

When there's no time for a long prayer, His name is enough. "I will set him on high, because he has known My name." God "has given Him the name which is above every name": above cancer, accident and death. At the name of Jesus every knee must bow.

messages.text: The Bible never says you have an appointed time to die. It says, "It is appointed for men to die once." And some things lengthen your days.
messages.explanation:
"When it's your time, it's your time" isn't Scripture. Hebrews says it's appointed for men to die once, not at a fixed hour. Lazarus died twice, and the generation alive at the rapture won't die at all. Fate isn't in the Bible. Faith is.

Scripture does say some choices prolong life and some shorten it. "The fear of the Lord prolongs days": worshipping Him adds to your life. Honouring your parents brings long life; a lying tongue "is but for a moment." Living in sin with no desire to change drains life away. That's why John says, "If anyone sees his brother sinning… he will ask, and He will give him life."

messages.text: "As your God, I judge the world. As your Father, I judge no one."
messages.explanation:
Jesus said, "The Father judges no one." God will judge the nations, but to His children He is Father, and the Father isn't sitting in judgment over you. There's a revival of interest in the Hebrew names of God, and they're precious. But the name above them, the one Jesus came to reveal, is "Father": Abba, Daddy.

Listen to how you pray. "O God… O God" can carry a sense of distance; anyone can say "God." "Father" speaks of nearness. Psalm 91 ends with two conditions: "Because he has set his love upon Me" and "because he has known My name." Know Him as Father, and love His Son.

messages.text: Three of David's men broke through enemy lines just to bring him a drink from Bethlehem's well. God recorded their names. Joab, his army commander, isn't on the list.
messages.explanation:
Hiding in the cave of Adullam, David sighed, "Oh, that someone would give me a drink of the water from the well of Bethlehem!" Three mighty men risked their lives through a Philistine garrison simply because they loved him. Their deed is written in Scripture's list of David's mighty men, while Joab, who fought many battles for his own advancement, is missing.

A woman broke an alabaster flask worth a year's wages over Jesus' head. The disciples called it waste. Jesus said that wherever the gospel is preached, what she did will be told as a memorial to her. Big or small doesn't matter. What's done out of love for Jesus is what lasts.

messages.text: To the woman at the well, Jesus promised a well. At the feast, He promised rivers. A well is for you; rivers are for everyone around you.
messages.explanation:
In John 4 the drinking is a one-time act: drink once, and a well springs up inside you to everlasting life. That's the new birth. In John 7, on the last great day of the feast, Jesus cried, "If anyone thirsts, let him come to Me and drink," and the Greek is continuous: keep coming, keep drinking. Then "out of his heart will flow rivers of living water." John explains that He spoke of the Spirit.

In Jesus' day, a man could own a well, but rivers belonged to everyone. You can be saved and still be no blessing to anyone around you. When the rivers flow, "everything will live wherever the river goes," as Ezekiel saw the river from the temple bring even the Dead Sea to life.

messages.text: At Pentecost there was wind and fire. In the rest of Acts, those receiving the Spirit didn't always see wind or fire, but they always spoke.
messages.explanation:
The common denominator when people were filled with the Spirit in Acts was speaking: in tongues, or prophesying. "They began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance." They spoke; the Spirit gave the words. God won't force your mouth open. Evil spirits drive; the Holy Spirit leads. When the strange words come, speak them out.

Paul says, "Be filled with the Spirit, speaking to one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs." Then he goes straight on to husbands, wives, children and work. A Spirit-filled life is the oil in the machinery of marriage. Pray in the Spirit, and you'll find you're keeping yourself in the love of God.

messages.text: "He who speaks in a tongue edifies himself": he charges himself up like a battery. And how much you charge is up to you.
messages.explanation:
Nobody shows off their phone while it charges. It happens quietly, usually at night. Praying in tongues is like that: unglamorous, but you come out charged and ready to meet whatever negative situation you find. Some think they can only pray in tongues when the music is playing and the Spirit is moving. But Paul said, "I will pray with the spirit." It's a choice, any time, as long as you like.

Why is it so powerful? The temple had an outer court, a holy place and a most holy place. You're body, soul and spirit. Praying with your understanding is praying from the holy place. "If I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays," from the most holy place where God dwells. That's how you build yourself up "on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit."

messages.text: "The Spirit also helps in our weaknesses." The Greek pictures Him taking hold together with you, against the problem.
messages.explanation:
"We do not know what we should pray for as we ought." Paul included himself. Your baby won't stop crying and the doctor says it's normal. You don't know exactly what's wrong. But the Spirit does, and He "makes intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered": not in any language you know.

The word for "helps" is sunantilambanetai: sun (together with), anti (against), lambanō (take hold). He doesn't do it all while you do nothing. When you take hold of the problem by praying in the Spirit, He takes hold with you, and together you shift it. When you let go, He lets go. Pray until there's a release, a quiet peace that you've prayed through.

messages.text: On the highway, he felt a sense of danger and prayed in the Spirit until peace came. Minutes later, a truck crossed into his lane.
messages.explanation:
A minister was driving with his wife asleep beside him when an unease came over him. He prayed quietly in tongues, eyes open, until he sensed a release. Soon after, a truck lost control and came into his lane. He swerved, and it smashed into the small car behind him, crushing the driver's side. When he ran back, he found the driver unhurt, sitting in the passenger seat with no idea how he got there. The Spirit whispered, "This is what you were praying for."

You don't have to be on your knees, and you don't have to understand every word. If you knew everything the Spirit was praying, you might lock your children indoors for five years! Just pray, while cooking, driving, or sitting in a meeting, until peace comes.

messages.text: "With stammering lips and another tongue He will speak to this people… This is the rest… and this is the refreshing." Yet they would not hear.
messages.explanation:
Paul quotes Isaiah when he writes about tongues. Centuries earlier, God foresaw a gift for His people: rest for the weary and refreshing for the soul. He also foresaw that many would refuse it. You can often gauge how powerful a truth is by how fiercely it's opposed, and churches have split over this simple gift.

"Let us be diligent to enter that rest." At first, praying in tongues can feel like labour. Keep going. Inner fears, knots of anxiety and panic, things even your spouse doesn't know about, are like logs and rubbish clogging a river. The longer it flows, the more it clears, until it runs free. A running river is clean, refreshing, and it generates power.

messages.text: God designed your spirit to lead, your soul to follow, and your body to serve. That's what it means to be truly together.
messages.explanation:
When Adam sinned, his spirit died: cut off from God. Since then, people tend to live either from the mind, so clever they reason God out of everything, or from the body, driven by appetite. When you're born again, your spirit comes alive, but it starts as a baby while your mind has been in charge for years. When you pray in tongues, your mind says, "This is nonsense. Stop!"

Keep praying. Eventually the mind surrenders, not destroyed but enhanced, becoming the servant it was meant to be. Experienced fishermen who'd caught nothing all night had every reason to argue with a carpenter. When they let down the nets at His word, the nets broke with fish. Let your spirit lead.

messages.text: "Wait for the Promise of the Father." Among thousands of promises, the disciples knew which one He meant.
messages.explanation:
Jesus' disciples had spent three and a half years watching Him heal the sick and raise the dead, the best Bible school there ever was. Yet He told them not to go out and preach yet, but to wait for the Promise: the Holy Spirit. "You shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you shall be witnesses to Me." Not just do witnessing, but be witnesses: your very presence becomes a testimony.

What Jesus valued that much is not an optional extra. When the Spirit came, "they began to speak with other tongues." Some churches stop teaching it so as not to scare newcomers. But in the early church, newcomers were ushered straight into God's power. Don't settle for less than the Bible's standard.

messages.text: When you pray in English, you can pray selfishly or amiss. When the Spirit prays through you, He always prays according to the will of God.
messages.explanation:
"He who searches the hearts knows what the mind of the Spirit is, because He makes intercession for the saints according to the will of God." Your understanding is limited; you can only pray about what you know. In tongues you can pray for your future, for your children's future, for people you haven't even met.

And John says, "If we ask anything according to His will, He hears us… we know that we have the petitions that we have asked of Him." Prayer in the Spirit is always in His will, so it's always heard. Sometimes problems vanish at once; sometimes you receive wisdom to handle them, or strength to go through. But something good always happens.

messages.text: His little girl woke screaming and wouldn't be comforted. He sat on the bathroom floor and said, "Holy Spirit, You know what's wrong." After one line in tongues, she stopped crying.
messages.explanation:
Jessica, Joseph Prince's young daughter, woke up frightened and crying, though she wasn't sick or feverish. Nothing her parents did could calm her. He went to the bathroom, sat down and asked the Spirit to pray through him. He'd barely begun when the crying in the next room stopped.

That's not always how it goes. More often you pray until you feel a release: a lightness, a peace, a quiet note of victory. Another pastor's daughter had a stomach virus the doctor said would last at least three days; he laid hands on her and prayed in tongues for some time, and she was asking for food on the way home. Pray until the release comes.

messages.text: Picture a triangle with Jesus at the top. As husband and wife each move closer to Him, they move closer to each other.
messages.explanation:
When two people look only at each other, each eventually demands what only God can give: more time, more understanding, more appreciation. They drain each other dry. Marriage was God's idea, long before the church, and He designed it with a third party: Jesus, by His Spirit. You can throw every burden on Him, and He only gets stronger.

Paul says "be filled with the Spirit… singing and making melody in your heart," before he says a word to wives and husbands. The Spirit is the oil that keeps the machinery running without sparks. Let both of you draw near to Jesus, and the distance between you shrinks.

messages.text: Living with someone who gets on your nerves? Pray in the Spirit under your breath, and you'll keep yourself in the love of God.
messages.explanation:
It could be an in-law, an elderly relative, a housemate. You've forgiven them ten thousand times and asked God for love, yet you still end up frustrated with how they do things or what they say. Let's be honest: some people are channels of friction.

Jude writes, "Building yourselves up on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit, keep yourselves in the love of God." When they do that irritating thing again, don't fight it in your own strength. Pray quietly in tongues. It's a grace gift for exactly that moment, and it keeps your heart soft toward them.

messages.text: "I speak in tongues more than you all; yet in the church I would rather speak five words with my understanding, that I may teach others also." Also.
messages.explanation:
Paul isn't downplaying tongues; he thanks God he prays in tongues more than all of them. In private, ten thousand words; in public, five words people can understand. And notice "that I may teach others also." He's implying that he himself was taught while praying in the Spirit. Five words, "Stand up straight on your feet," and a man crippled from birth leapt up.

Paul says when he comes to you, it should be with "revelation, or knowledge, or prophesying, or teaching." Those flow out of time spent praying in the Spirit. Before a job interview, a counselling chat over coffee, a hard conversation, pray in tongues on the way. You may say something wiser than you are.

messages.text: "The shield of faith, with which you will be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked one." A wooden shield would catch fire. You quench fire with water.
messages.explanation:
Joseph Prince had always pictured a Roman shield, until the Lord drew his attention to two words: "quench" and "fiery." Burning arrows set wooden shields alight. Then, in an inward vision, he saw a shield of water around a believer, and every flaming dart that struck it was extinguished.

Where does that water come from? "Out of his heart will flow rivers of living water." As you pray in the Spirit, those rivers surround you. You don't have to address the devil all the time. Just keep talking to God in the Spirit, and the enemy feels the effect.
